claims.head: Who blinks first?
claims.body: The Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Avalanche are the best at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Penguins still get theirs.
claims.call: The Penguins’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Avalanche.
claims.nums: Pittsburgh 3rd for chance quality (a 6.9% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Colorado 1st for preventing dangerous shots

claims.head: The Avalanche will send Toews and Makar at Crosby
claims.call: The Avalanche’s P1 (Toews and Makar) spends at least 53% of its 5-on-5 time against the Penguins’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Avalanche keep sending Toews and Makar out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jared Bednar has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Penguins’ first line is Crosby, Rust and Rakell.
claims.nums: At home: 53% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 39% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Jared Bednar likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Penguins’ first line.

claims.head: Shots should fly both ways

claims.body: Pittsburgh plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Colorado. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.

claims.head: In close against from distance
claims.body: The Penguins get in close, but the Avalanche mostly shoot from distance. Pittsburgh is the league’s best for shots from in close, and Colorado is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Penguins to do more of their damage around the net.

notes.text: Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Spencer Stastney has taken his spot beside Kris Letang.
Spencer Stastney joined from EDM on Oct 7.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 3 of their last 7 games, including the last one. Fedor Svechkov takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Noah Juulsen is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Kulak and Malinski.
T.J. Hughes is day to day, reported after he played in their last game.
Gavin Brindley was added to the roster on Oct 15 and has played beside Parker Kelly and Fedor Svechkov.
Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.

COL.head: The matchup suits the Avalanche
COL.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Penguins’ way back in is a penalty kill that holds up.

PIT.head: The Penguins face a real test
PIT.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Penguins can pull it off if their penalty kill holds up.

story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Penguins come in at 3-3-1, the Avalanche at 4-2-1.

It’s strength against strength: the Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Avalanche are the best at preventing dangerous shots. At home, Jared Bednar likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Pens’ first line.
